note: NOISY BOY. The purple samurai: a deep violet shell, yellow trim and
kanji panels, a pointed helmet with lit eyes, and two big yellow LED
displays on the gauntlets. Painted off the reference photograph.
Measured off his own rig, in the boxing stance the file is stored in:
THE KANJI ARE NOT REPRODUCED. There are a dozen glyphs on the chest
and the shoulders of the reference and none of them survive being
drawn with vertex colours on an eighteen-thousand-vertex mesh — the
smallest stroke is thinner than the triangles are wide. What carries
the character at any distance he is ever seen from is the pairing:
deep purple with yellow panels in bands across the chest, which the
decals do give. Trying for the glyphs themselves buys nothing and
costs the clean read of the bands.
THE GAUNTLET PANELS ARE PICKED BY `ax` AND NOT BY DEPTH. They face
outward, and he is stored with his guard up — both forearms angled
across his chest — so the panel's own normal points sideways and the
front-facing test that works on his chest finds nothing at all on his
arms. |x| is what separates the outside of a gauntlet from the inside
in this pose, and it is stable under the stance because both arms are
in the same one.
THE EYES ARE THE FACE OVERLAY, which works here because this rig does
have a Head bone with the helmet weighted to it — Ambush's does not.
